title: Blood Gases, Pulse Oximetry, and Capnography

source.boundary: Actual Chapter16 title lower right PDF26/printed78, below Chapter15 REFERENCES notice; through Figure16-2, left-column concluding prose and right-column REFERENCES notice PDF29/printed81, above actual Chapter17 title. Chapter17 running header on PDF29 is not a boundary.

scope: Thirteen selected reusable vocabulary terms, not exhaustive chapter coverage. Offline candidate associations only, not clinical lessons, anchors, narration or image-generation prompts. New compositions mean newly recorded combinations, not invented primitives or claims of novelty.

entries.cue: A small seaside tide washing into a clear water pitcher.
entries.prior: New composition using docs/visual-cue-catalog.json#water-pitcher; tide is a newly recorded familiar ingredient, not a proprietary primitive.
entries.reason: Familiar tide and container association, not a whole-name sound puzzle. Water volume is wordplay, not a lung model, breathing measurement or fluid instruction.

entries.cue: An empty unused room cordoned off from a busy neighboring room.
entries.prior: new_chapter_record; ordinary unused-room relationship, not a previously established primitive in the checked banks
entries.reason: Dead space is familiar everyday language. Physiologic qualifier is supplied by lesson context; no lung anatomy, gas-exchange explanation or fraction is encoded.

entries.cue: Clear water pitcher with a small pool left at the bottom after pouring.
entries.prior: New composition of docs/visual-cue-catalog.json#water-pitcher with familiar remaining-contents relationship.
entries.reason: Partial learned cue for residual, not a complete definition of functional or capacity. Do not mistake this generic leftover-water metaphor for a lung measurement, respiratory phase or fluid recommendation.

entries.cue: A desk fan beside an analog clock with its minute hand conspicuous.
entries.prior: new_chapter_record; familiar clock and fan composition, not a newly invented primitive
entries.reason: Familiar clock/fan pairing can be learned without a syllable puzzle. Minute-hand recognition needs context; no elapsed duration, breathing rate, formula or clinical setting is specified.

entries.cue: Fan token and water-pump token mounted on two visibly nonmatching puzzle pieces.
entries.prior: New composition; fan ingredient shared with minute ventilation in this bank, pump is a familiar supply token.
entries.reason: Mismatch is carried by the failed fit, not an arbitrary color code. Perfusion/pump association must be taught; this is not a circulation schematic, mechanism or explanation of either clinical mismatch pattern.

entries.cue: Recognizable finger-clip pulse oximeter with an unnumbered display.
entries.prior: new_chapter_record; familiar device, not a newly invented primitive
entries.reason: Device category is sufficient in lesson context without a full-word rebus. No reading, interpretation, accuracy, diagnostic criterion or placement instruction is supplied.

entries.cue: Familiar ship captain pointing to a simple line graph on a chart.
entries.cue_scope: Colloquial cap'n plus graph name bridge
entries.prior: new_chapter_record; new captain/graph composition of ordinary ingredients
entries.reason: Cap'n/graph is a learned partial-name association, not an assertion of exact pronunciation. Chart is not a capnogram or a clinical waveform. No thresholds, gas sampling or interpretation encoded.

entries.cue: Magnifying glass over the broad main channel of a small stream model.
entries.prior: new_chapter_record; new stream/search composition, paired with side stream detector
entries.reason: Uses familiar stream double meaning and a learned search/detector token. Not a detector design, breathing circuit, sampling route or medical equipment specification.

entries.cue: Magnifying glass over a small side branch of the same stream model.
entries.prior: New contrast composition sharing stream and magnifying-glass ingredients with mainstream detector in this bank.
entries.reason: Keep the same stream layout and change the inspected branch only. Branch relationship encodes the words, not an airway sampling diagram or equipment comparison.

entries.cue: Blood-drop character beside a nearly empty oxygen tank.
entries.reason: Preserves prior cue and oxygen-cylinder family. Tank quantity is metaphorical, not a blood measurement, diagnostic threshold, causal claim or oxygen-treatment instruction.

entries.cue: Familiar milk bottle beside a small puddle of milk.
entries.reason: Reuses milk/lact- without adding an acid puzzle. Not a claim about milk, lactate origins, physiology or a clinical laboratory interpretation.

entries.cue: Familiar orange baking-soda box with a small heap of white powder; no brand logo or answer label needed.
entries.prior: docs/chapter-2-cue-audit.json#sodium bicarbonate and docs/chapter-12-cue-audit.json; same bicarbonate family primitive, user calibration takes precedence over narrower catalog caution
entries.reason: Unqualified bicarbonate shares the established baking-soda cue. Does not supply sodium qualifier to the source, a chemical formula, medication formulation, household-use permission or clinical instruction.

entries.prior: Main proposed after initial author hold; author independently challenged and retained under broad user partial-name calibration. New composition using familiar carb-food and established overflow relationship, not a new primitive.
entries.reason: Familiar carb plus visible excess is economical without a whole-word syllable puzzle. Collides with high-carb meals and hyperglycemia; lesson context must supply hypercarbia. Not a claim that food causes carbon dioxide retention, an identification of blood gas content, a mechanism or a diet recommendation. Conceptual author challenge only, no empirical or rendered validation.
